newsitem.title: USA: Survivors of Nashville crash victims sue U.S..
newsitem.headline: Survivors of Nashville crash victims sue U.S..

text.p: Survivors of three people killed in the crash of a Navy F-14 jet plane in Nashville early this year filed lawsuits on Monday seeking about $16 million from the U.S. government, a spokeswoman for a law firm said.

The lawsuit was filed by relatives of Elmer and Ada Newsome and of Ewing Wair Sr., in U.S. District Court, with the plaintiffs seeking about $12 million in the Newsome deaths and about $4 million in the Wair death, said Anna Wheeler of the Sabin R. Thompson law firm.
Wair was a guest in the Newsome home on Jan. 29, when a U.S. Navy F-14 crashed into it, killing all three.
The pilot of the plane, Lt. Cmdr. Stacy Bates, lost control of his plane as he left Nashville's airport. He died in the crash, along with his co-pilot.
Families of the victims accused Bates of pilot negligence. They asked for damages on three counts, the wrongful death of the victims and infliction of negligent and intentional emotional distress.

The suits claimed the Navy failed to train and supervise Bates properly and that he performed an unnecessary high-risk manoeuvre taking off from the airport. They also noted that Bates had crashed another F-14 some months earlier.
